subChunks.title: Building a Card Component
subChunks.hookHtml: The Card is the fundamental content container of modern web UI — it groups related information, creates visual hierarchy, and provides a consistent canvas for data presentation. Building cards well means knowing how to handle images, titles, body text, badges, and action buttons in a constrained space.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Card anatomy

/* Basic card shell */
bg-white rounded-xl shadow-sm border border-gray-100
overflow-hidden  /* clip images to card corners */

/* Card with hover interaction */
bg-white rounded-xl shadow-sm border border-gray-100
hover:shadow-md hover:-translate-y-0.5
transition duration-200 cursor-pointer

Vertical card (image + content)

<div class="bg-white rounded-xl shadow-sm overflow-hidden max-w-sm">
  <!-- Image section -->
  <div class="aspect-video overflow-hidden">
    <img class="w-full h-full object-cover hover:scale-105 transition-transform duration-300"
         src="/quest-banner.jpg" alt="Quest Banner" />
  </div>

  <!-- Content section -->
  <div class="p-5">
    <!-- Badge -->
    <span class="bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700 text-xs font-semibold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full">
      Active
    </span>

    <h3 class="font-semibold text-gray-900 mt-2 leading-snug">Slay the Dragon</h3>
    <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-1 line-clamp-2">
      A legendary quest through the Ember Mountains.
    </p>

    <!-- Footer -->
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between mt-4 pt-4 border-t border-gray-100">
      <span class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-900">500 XP</span>
      <button class="text-sm text-blue-600 hover:text-blue-700 font-medium">
        Accept →
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Horizontal card (avatar + content)

<div class="flex gap-4 items-start bg-white rounded-xl p-5 shadow-sm border border-gray-100">
  <img class="w-12 h-12 rounded-full flex-none object-cover" src="/avatar.jpg" alt="Aria" />
  <div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
    <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
      <h3 class="font-semibold text-gray-900 truncate">Aria Sunforge</h3>
      <span class="text-xs text-gray-400 ml-2 flex-none">2h ago</span>
    </div>
    <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-0.5 line-clamp-2">
      Completed the Dragon Quest and earned the Ember Badge.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>

Stat card

<div class="bg-white rounded-xl p-6 shadow-sm border border-gray-100">
  <div class="flex items-center justify-between">
    <span class="text-sm font-medium text-gray-500">Total Quests</span>
    <div class="w-8 h-8 bg-blue-100 rounded-lg flex items-center justify-center">
      <svg class="w-4 h-4 text-blue-600">...</svg>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="text-3xl font-bold text-gray-900 mt-2">1,247</p>
  <p class="text-sm text-emerald-600 mt-1">↑ 12% from last month</p>
</div>

Lyra: "Cards have a hierarchy: badge → title → description → actions. Follow this order in the HTML and the visual weight falls naturally. The button in the card footer should never be a primary blue — inside a card, it should be a ghost or link style. The card itself is the primary visual element; the button is a secondary call to action."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: A card is a microcosm of everything you have learned. Spacing, typography, colour, borders, images, buttons, overflow, flexbox — they all compose into one cohesive unit. Get the card right, and you have proven your understanding of the whole system.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a complete quest card with all sections properly styled:

  • .quest-card: white background, rounded-xl, shadow-sm, overflow-hidden, max-w-sm, border, border-gray-100, hover lift effect, transition
  • .quest-banner: w-full, aspect-video, object-cover
  • .quest-badge: emerald background/text, text-xs, font-semibold, rounded-full, px-2, py-0.5
  • .quest-title: font-semibold, text-gray-900, mt-2, leading-snug
  • .quest-desc: text-sm, text-gray-500, mt-1, line-clamp-2
  • .quest-footer: flex, items-center, justify-between, mt-4, pt-4, border-t, border-gray-100

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a member profile card from scratch (no guided classes): a circular avatar, a name (truncated), a role badge, a bio (3 lines clamped), a stats row (quests completed and XP), and two buttons — a primary 'Message' and a ghost 'View Profile'. Apply a hover lift effect on the whole card. Everything from memory.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through every class on a complete quest card and explain what it does. Pay particular attention to overflow-hidden and why it is necessary, aspect-video on the image, and line-clamp-2 on the description. Why should the action button inside a card be ghost style rather than primary blue?

questions.prompt: A card has rounded-xl and an image at the top. The image's corners don't respect the card's rounding — they appear squared. What is the fix?
options: overflow-hidden on the card — this clips child elements (including the image) to the card's border-radius
rounded-tl-xl rounded-tr-xl on the image to round its top corners
border-radius on the image matching the card's rounded-xl value
object-cover clips the image to the card shape automatically
questions.answer: overflow-hidden on the card — this clips child elements (including the image) to the card's border-radius
questions.explanation: border-radius creates the rounded visual shape, but child elements with background content can still bleed outside it without overflow-hidden. Adding overflow-hidden to the card clips all child content (including images) to the card's border-radius. This is why overflow-hidden is a standard part of any card component that contains images.

questions.prompt: A card grid shows three cards in a row. Card 1 has a 2-line description; Card 3 has an 8-line description. The 'Accept' buttons need to align at the bottom of each card regardless of description length. Which approach fixes this?
options: Make each card flex-col, then add mt-auto to the card footer — mt-auto pushes the footer to the card bottom in a flex column
Add a fixed height to the description section (h-20) to equalise card heights
Use position-absolute bottom-0 on the footer within a position-relative card
Add items-end to the parent grid container
questions.answer: Make each card flex-col, then add mt-auto to the card footer — mt-auto pushes the footer to the card bottom in a flex column
questions.explanation: In a grid with align-items: stretch (the default), all cards in a row stretch to the same height. Adding flex flex-col to each card and mt-auto to the footer pushes the footer to the card's bottom, regardless of how much content is above it. The description area expands naturally without a fixed height.

questions.prompt: You are building a member directory. Each member card shows an avatar, name, role, and stats. You need 3 cards per row on desktop and 1 per row on mobile. Which parent class pattern achieves this before learning Grid?
options: flex flex-wrap gap-4 with each card having w-full sm:w-auto flex-1 — wrap means cards flow to new lines when needed
flex gap-4 with w-1/3 on each card — divides width equally into thirds
inline-flex on the parent with w-96 on each card
questions.answer: flex flex-wrap gap-4 with each card having w-full sm:w-auto flex-1 — wrap means cards flow to new lines when needed
questions.explanation: flex-wrap allows flex children to wrap to the next line when the container is too narrow. On mobile (w-full per card), each card takes a full row. On larger screens (sm:w-auto flex-1), cards share the row. This is a flex-based approximation of a responsive grid, though CSS Grid (covered in the Junior tier) is the more precise tool for this layout.
